# Red test before fix

<!-- review-bot-scope:start -->
packages/*/src/**/*.ts
packages/*/test/**/*.ts
scripts/*.py
scripts/*.sh
postmortems/*.md
<!-- review-bot-scope:end -->

Scope: `packages/*/src/**/*.ts`, `packages/*/test/**/*.ts`, `scripts/*.py`, `scripts/*.sh`, `postmortems/*.md`. This rule judges one thing: whether a change that repairs a bug arrived with a test that could have **failed against the broken code**. It does not judge whether the fix is correct (the fencing/provenance rules do that), whether a class-level tripwire was also instituted or sits at the right altitude (the prevention-mechanism rule), whether a postmortem's non-Evidence sections are complete (the postmortem rule), or whether a new protocol was TLC-verified before its SQL existed (the spec-first rule). New capability that never shipped a bug owes no red test and is deliberately outside this rule.

The invariant is CLAUDE.md's standing rule: every bug fix lands as two commits — a regression test run and **seen failing**, then the fix that turns it green — and if a bug cannot be expressed as a red test, that is a missing seam and the seam is built first. The seams exist for exactly this: pinned `SimWorld`/`Rng` seeds for interleavings, `admin.setFakeNowEpochMs` for time, raw fixture SQL through `f.raw.batch` for states the fences make unreachable, `seededIdSource` id/token sequences for deliberate collisions, `buggify` for legal-rare paths, and `FencedBatch`'s construction checks. The reason this is a hard rule and not a preference is arithmetic: across the 44 findings of `postmortems/pr3.6-fence-provenance.md`, this project's automated machinery — 236 fault-matrix cells, 32 fuzz shards, a TLC model of 111.8M states, an invariant library, nine checkers — found **zero**. Green proves the tests accept correct code and says nothing about whether they reject incorrect code.

Three incidents prove the specific failure. Finding 28: the regression pinning spawn's task-id collision collided on **both** the task id and the idempotency key, so the targeted `ON CONFLICT` absorbed it and the primary-key guard was never reached — and the call was `await f.store.spawn(Q, 'job', '{}', { idempotencyKey: 'k' }).catch(() => {})`, after which the only assertions were "no runs exist" and "the task is still completed", both of which hold when spawn throws. Deleting the guard broke nothing. Finding 33: the emit correlation guard became a `wake_event` match plus a `wake_step` match, and the single regression was satisfied by **either half**, so deleting either kept the suite green. Finding 42: the emit's query-plan pin `EXPLAIN`ed a statement hand-copied into the test as "structurally the same" — deleting the entire index driver from the shipped statement left the plan suite green while every emit fell back to scanning the runs table. In all three the test existed, was reviewed, and could not go red.

<!-- review-bot-synopsis:start -->
Flag a repair whose test lands with no preceding test-only commit and no stated observed failure, or a test that survives reverting the fix — the swallowed call whose rejection the fix changes followed only by assertions a throw also satisfies, an existence-only assertion as the whole test, a fixture that reaches a pre-existing conflict clause before the new guard, one case for a two-conjunct guard or a generated surface varying one side of the correlation, a plan/text pin on SQL re-typed into the test while the shipped statement is exported or recoverable — plus any assertion deleted/loosened/skipped or pinned seed, id/token sequence or fake-now value moved in the fix's own commit, a deleted mutation-probe entry, a broadened checker with no new lint-selftest bad fixture, an "untestable" claim with no seam, and an added postmortem whose Evidence names no red test for the findings fixed here. Pass for red+green pairs and combined commits quoting the failure they saw, fixes that strengthen or correct their own red test, new capability and construction-time red, existence assertions used as anti-vacuity preconditions, `.catch()` where the rejection is not the property under test, raw fixture SQL and deliberate negative controls, mutations re-aimed rather than deleted, mechanical test refactors, injected values corrected because a new oracle rejected them, checker fixes carrying their bad fixture, and comment-only source edits.
<!-- review-bot-synopsis:end -->

Report a failure when the changed code introduces or materially expands any of these. Each is decidable from the diff plus the commit list; where only a squashed diff is visible, judge the whole change as one commit.

- A behavior-changing edit under `packages/*/src/**` that the commit message, a code comment, or a postmortem row calls a repair ("bug", "defect", "finding", "regression", "no longer", "was wrong", "used to"), where no earlier commit on the branch is test-only (touching only `packages/*/test/**`, `packages/conformance/src/`, `scripts/lint-selftest.py`, or `scripts/mutation-probe.py`) and adds or extends the case that pins it. Red commits here carry no marker — round 6's are `b55032f`, `d166c65`, `fcc7cfa`, all plain-language subjects — so identify them by content, never by a `RED:` prefix.
- The fix and its test in one commit whose message names no observed failure: no assertion text, state, or error the pre-fix code produced.
- A test that still passes with the source hunk reverted, by vacuity. Three decidable forms: (a) the call whose rejection or return value the fix changes is wrapped in `.catch(() => {})`, or a `.catch` whose captured error is never asserted on, and every remaining assertion also holds if that call throws at its first statement (zero counts, fixture state unchanged) — this is finding 28; (b) the test body's only assertion is existence or truthiness (`toBeDefined`, `toBeTruthy`, `not.toThrow`); (c) the asserted rows or columns are ones no statement in the source diff writes.
- A case whose fixture satisfies the new condition **together with** a clause that fires first — a targeted `ON CONFLICT`, an earlier disjunct, an outer guard — so the added condition is dead and deleting it changes nothing. Decidable whenever the statement is in the diff; it is the other half of finding 28.
- A fix that adds a conjunct to a predicate with one accompanying case that each conjunct satisfies alone, and no case that only the new conjunct rules out (finding 33). Likewise a generated fault surface or fixture set that varies only one side of the correlation the fix constrains, so every generated case already satisfies the new condition (finding 43).
- A pin on a **second representation**: a test that `EXPLAIN`s, executes, or text-matches a statement re-typed into the test file when the shipped one is reachable — exported (`NEXT_WAKE_SQL`, `SWEEP_SCAN_CANCELS_SQL`, `SWEEP_SCAN_EXPIRED_SQL`) or recoverable by running the real operation through a recording executor, as `shippedWakeStatement()` in `packages/store-libsql/test/query-plans.test.ts` now does. Such a pin cannot go red when the shipped statement changes (finding 42).
- In the fix's own commit, an existing assertion deleted, narrowed, or disabled — an `expect` removed, `toEqual([...])` relaxed to a matcher that accepts more, `toBe` loosened to `toBeTruthy`, `it` changed to `it.skip`/`it.todo`, a timeout raised, or a `try`/`catch` wrapped around the asserted call — with no sentence naming the assertion that stayed red and why the edit is a correction rather than a retreat.
- In the fix's own commit, a pinned `SimWorld`/`Rng` seed, a `seededIdSource` id or token sequence, an injected duplicate/crash label, or a `setFakeNowEpochMs`/advance value changed inside a test that pins a bug, with no sentence saying what the old values produced and why the new ones still produce it.
- A `scripts/mutation-probe.py` entry for the guard being changed **deleted** with no entry left covering that guard, or a `BAD_CASES` fixture removed from `scripts/lint-selftest.py`.
- An existing checker under `scripts/` changed to match a spelling or case it previously missed, with no `BAD_CASES` entry added that the pre-change checker accepted. The bug in a checker is always in what its pattern did *not* match, which reading source is worst at. (A brand-new checker needs no finding here: `lint-selftest.py` already refuses any lint with no bad case.)
- A message, comment, or postmortem line claiming a bug is untestable, hard to reproduce, or "covered by the types now", with no seam added in the same change. That claim is the rule's trigger, not its excuse.
- A `postmortems/*.md` added or extended in this diff whose Evidence section lists no red tests at all, or lists none covering the findings whose fixes are in this diff — individually or by a stated group ("the port and primitive tests for findings 23, 24 and 25" is sufficient). Round 6's per-finding form is the target: `` `b55032f` (finding 39, "expected 'cancelled' to be 'running'") ``.

Allowed cases (do NOT flag these):

- **A fix commit correcting its own red test's secondary assertion.** `76b7835` changed `expect(await engineInvariantViolations(f.raw)).toEqual([])` to `.toEqual(before)` in `packages/conformance/test/replay-after-the-world-moved.test.ts` — the fixture is deliberately corrupt, so an empty-violations assertion failed for the wrong reason. The assertion seen red (`expect(after?.state).toBe('sleeping')`) is untouched and the message says which.
- **A fix commit strengthening its red test.** `f434586`, same file, replaced `toEqual(before)` with `toEqual(expect.arrayContaining(before))` (line 385) and added a `toContain('wait-for-fired-event: …')`. Adding assertions is not weakening, even when a matcher is technically broadened.
- **A combined commit that quotes what it saw fail.** `a79f7ff` (`RED+GREEN: a task's unserializable event payload is a task failure, not an outage`) states which assertion failed and why the halves are inseparable; it also deleted an earlier regression's self-contradictory pair ("asserted both that no runs exist and that the reported run id exists in runs. No implementation can satisfy both") — a correction, not a retreat. `6dd24a9` lands 52 test lines and a 3-line `store.ts` guard in one unlabelled commit and justifies it in prose ("The regression test fails without the guard and passes with it"); that is the accepted shape.
- **New capability, and construction-time red.** `29d95fe` added `packages/conformance/test/wake-witness-surface.test.ts` with no accompanying fix. Likewise the paired accept/reject units in `packages/core/test/fenced-batch.test.ts`, where `expect(() => withCas()).not.toThrow()` (line 83) is the accept side of a rejection test and red is a thrown construction error.
- **Existence assertions used as anti-vacuity preconditions.** `expect(run).toBeDefined()` before `if (!run) return`, with the discriminating assertions after — `packages/conformance/src/suite.ts:183` and `:196` (whose comment says a bare `if (!run) return` "would make this test pass VACUOUSLY"), and `packages/sdk/test/user-boundary.test.ts:70`. Flag only when such an assertion is the whole test.
- **`.catch()` where the rejection is not the property under test.** `packages/conformance/test/regressions.test.ts:160` (`complete(...).catch(() => {})`, then `expect(task.state).toBe('cancelled')`) and `:440`; `packages/store-libsql/test/await-event-regressions.test.ts:148`; `packages/sdk/test/review-regressions.test.ts:96,102,131,165,250` (store-outage proxies, then attempts/state assertions); `packages/sdk/test/replay-equivalence.test.ts:286`; `packages/conformance/test/fence-provenance-regressions.test.ts:412`, with `:212` and `:248` capturing the rejection and asserting on it. Flag only when the fix changes whether or what that call throws — the shape `regressions.test.ts:238` calls out in a comment ("Deliberately NOT wrapped in `.catch()`").
- **Hand-written SQL that is not a second representation.** Raw fixture SQL through `f.raw.batch` is the sanctioned seam for building states the fences make unreachable (throughout `regressions.test.ts` and `generated-selection.test.ts`). So is a deliberate negative control: `query-plans.test.ts`'s "degrades to a full scan if the waiter subquery is correlated" hand-writes the bad shape precisely so the pin above it is known to discriminate.
- **A mutation re-aimed rather than deleted.** `514dcf5` ("Move two mutations from the call sites to the generator") and `be6aac5` ("Re-aim two mutations at the SQL they now protect") followed refactors that moved the guard; `mutation-probe.py:261` reports a stale pattern as a survivor, so re-aiming is the maintenance the mechanism demands.
- **Mechanical test-only refactors.** `a5f145b` rewrote 18 test files onto `openTestDb` from `packages/store-libsql/src/testing.ts` without changing what any of them assert.
- **Injected-value corrections a new oracle found, when stated.** `b35101b` changed `token: () => tok-${n}` to `token: () => tok-${++seeds}` in `legacy-rows.test.ts` and `replay-after-the-world-moved.test.ts` in the same commit that added the `one-batch-two-instants` invariant, explaining that a shared counter hands two consecutive batches the same seed. A pinned input edited **because** a new checker rejected it, with that said in the message, is a correction.
- **A checker fix carrying its bad fixture in the same commit.** `8dd33f6` changed `clock-lint.py` and `fragment-lint.py` and added `BAD_CASES` entries alongside; the fixture *is* the executable red, since the self-test requires a nonzero exit the pre-change checker did not produce.
- **Comment-only edits to source, and documentation commits.** `cb72862` rewrote a comment block in `packages/store-libsql/src/store.ts` with no statement change.
- **Infrastructure postmortems whose fix is not in `packages/`.** `postmortems/nightly-2026-07-24-tlc-infra.md` evidences an authoritative reproduction rather than a red test; that is the right artifact for a tooling failure.

When you report, name the invariant (CLAUDE.md, "red test before fix") and then do the part that makes the finding actionable: state the exact assertion that would **still pass against the pre-fix code**, or say which of the two commits is missing. Then demand the mechanism rather than the fix — either the red commit with its observed failure quoted in the postmortem's Evidence form, or, where the test genuinely must land with the fix, a `scripts/mutation-probe.py` entry that deletes this guard and requires the suite to fail. If no seam can express the bug, say which seam is missing (a pinned `SimWorld`/`Rng` seed, `setFakeNowEpochMs`, raw fixture SQL, a seeded id/token sequence, `buggify`, a `FencedBatch` construction check) and why none fits; building that seam is the finding. A hosted reviewer is a detection net of last resort, never a rung on the prevention ladder — a finding that ends at "add a test next time" has patched the net instead of the hole, and this rule exists because three tests that already existed could not go red.
